title: Russian Ballistic Missile Barrage Kills 8, Wounds 37 Nationwide; Interpipe Plant in Dnipro Halted
detail: Russian forces launched a combined ballistic and cruise missile barrage overnight into September 22, killing at least 8 people and wounding 37 across Ukraine. The heaviest single strike hit the Interpipe steel and railway-products plant in Dnipro with ballistic missiles, killing 4 employees and forcing the 9,500-worker manufacturer to halt production; Interpipe said the strike 'damaged key production equipment and infrastructure.' Russian forces also struck industrial facilities in Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad the same night. Dnipropetrovsk Oblast recorded the highest regional toll at 5 killed and 7 wounded; Donetsk Oblast reported 1 killed and 11 wounded; Zaporizhzhia Oblast 1 killed and 9 wounded; Kharkiv Oblast 1 killed and 1 wounded; Kherson Oblast 6 wounded; and Kyiv 3 wounded. Fires were also reported in Zhytomyr, Odesa, and Kirovohrad oblasts. The attack package included Onyx anti-ship missiles, Iskander-M/S-400/KN-23 ballistic missiles, 4 Kalibr cruise missiles, 8 Banderol/Dan-T weapons, and 212 drones; Ukraine's Air Force said it downed or suppressed 186 of the aerial targets.

title: Ukraine Strikes Ufa's Bashneft-UNPZ and Samara's Kuibyshev Oil Refineries in Deep Drone Raids
detail: Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Bashneft-UNPZ oil refinery in Ufa, Republic of Bashkortostan (~1,300 km from the Ukrainian border) on September 21, and the Rosneft-operated Kuibyshev oil refinery in Samara Oblast (~910 km from the border) overnight into September 22, Ukraine's General Staff confirmed. Fires were reported at both facilities, which have annual processing capacities of roughly 7.5 million and 7 million metric tons respectively; the Kuibyshev plant had previously been hit in June 2026, temporarily halting oil processing. Ukraine's General Staff said 'products from both refineries are used to supply the Russian military,' framing the strikes as part of its sustained campaign against Russian fuel infrastructure supporting the invasion.

title: Zelensky Meets Trump at UN, Proposes Reciprocal Energy Ceasefire; Discusses Patriot Interceptor Licensing
detail: President Zelensky held closed-door talks with President Trump for roughly 40 minutes on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York on September 22. Zelensky said Ukraine is 'ready for energy ceasefire' in 'any kind of format,' proposing a reciprocal halt to strikes on energy infrastructure contingent on Russia agreeing to the same terms, and said Ukraine has received no unilateral order to stop its own strikes. The two leaders also discussed licensing Patriot interceptor production inside Ukraine; Zelensky said Trump did not reject the request, calling it 'a good step that nobody said no,' though he noted domestic production could take one to one-and-a-half years to establish and no concrete winter delivery commitments were announced. Trump said of a broader deal, 'I think we're gonna make a deal, and I don't want to say what the deal is.' Zelensky separately met UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham in New York the same day to discuss air defenses, winter preparations, and continued sanctions pressure on Moscow.
